aspects.says: A weakly consistent walk never throws and may or may not return an element added during it: in a ConcurrentHashMap that depends on whether the key lands in a bin the walk has passed, in a ConcurrentLinkedQueue a tail add made before the walk ends is seen.
basis: section:A Concurrent Add Is Seen or Missed by Where It Lands, So Walking and Then Clearing Loses Writes

aspects.says: A walk hands out entries read earlier, even ones removed since, so acting on one with remove(key) can remove a newer value; remove(key, value) removes only if the key still maps to the value checked.
basis: section:A Walk Hands Out Entries Read Earlier, So Act on One with remove(key, value)

aspects.says: A weakly consistent walk returns each element at most once, but an element removed and added again is a new element, so the same key or id can come twice, or a moved one can be missed.
basis: section:Each Element Comes at Most Once, but an Element Added Again Is a New One

aspects.says: size() and mappingCount() are readings taken at another moment than the walk, so an array sized by them and filled by a walk overflows or ends in nulls; the length must come from the walk.
basis: section:size() and a Walk Answer at Different Moments

aspects.says: Walking a concurrent map or queue and then calling clear() loses what arrived during and after the walk; taking each element out with remove(key) or poll() loses nothing.
basis: section:A Concurrent Add Is Seen or Missed by Where It Lands, So Walking and Then Clearing Loses Writes
